1. These two separate DARs were filed on 14.10.2020 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of
parties.
One Dar was prepared in respect of injuries sustained

Harsh Sharma driving his car bearing registration no. DL-4CAF-1395 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") at an excessive speed and in utter rash and negligent manner.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 9.
No bill regarding treatment has been filed.
It is common knowledge that generally people during the treatment do not maintain the bills etc as they are not aware of this benevolent legislation having provisions for compensation.
Keeping in view the overall circumstances, I hereby grant a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 10.
As per medical documents, the injured Tripti Kalra has suffered simple injuries.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which she actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate her for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.25,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said MACT No. 510/2020 Ravi Kalra Vs. Harsh Sharma period of her treatment and immobility.

sentences.text: Thus, she is awarded a total amount of Rs. 25,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of actual earnings 11.

In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner claims that she was working as a teacher at NRDPS,
Karala, Delhi and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month from that vocation at the time of accident.
The MLC and casualty ticket placed on record by petitioner reflect that the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries.
The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that she was unable to resume her work since the date of accident.
In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner could not have worked for about 03 months due to the injuries.
Petitioner has filed her Secondary School Examination Certificate Ex. PW-1/3 and certificate of cutting and sewing.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the Minimum Wages payable to a matriculate person in Delhi as on the date of accident.
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to a Matriculate Person as on 29.05.2019 in Delhi the earnings was Rs.17,508/-.As such
, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.52,524/- (Rs.17,508/- X 03).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb.
In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner could not have worked for about 06 months due to the injuries.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.1,05,048/- (Rs.17,508/- X 06).

(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 17.
Petitioner Ravi Kalra claimed in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he has become permanently disabled after the accident and could not perform his work by resuming his duties.

Admittedly,
petitioner Ravi Kalra has suffered 12% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb and same has a direct effect on the working capacity of a person impacting his future prospects.
Considering the same, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 12%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the monthly income of petitioner to be Rs.14,468/- at the relevant time.

As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned,
we may look into the photocopy of petitioner's Aadhar Card as per the said document, the date of birth of petitioner is 17.12.1972.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as MACT No. 510/2020 Ravi Kalra Vs. Harsh Sharma on the date of accident i.e. 29.05.2019 was around 46 years.

opennyai_summary.facts:
One Dar was prepared in respect of injuries sustained
As per petitioners, on 29.05.2019 at about 07:30 PM, they were travelling in hired OLA cab and going towards New Delhi Railway Station then the respondent had caused the accident near Burari Flyover, Delhi by MACT No. 510/2020 Ravi Kalra Vs. Harsh Sharma driving his car bearing registration no. DL-4CAF-1395 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") at an excessive speed and in utter rash and negligent manner.
Respondent had hit their cab resulting in massive accident and grievous injuries had been caused to them.
An FIR no. 0149/2019 U/s 279/338 IPC & 146/196 M.V. Act, PS Wazirabad,
was registered by the police with respect to above accident.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
1.1 As per injured Tripti Kalra, she sustained grievous injuries due to the aforesaid accident.
No bill regarding treatment has been filed.
Keeping in view the overall circumstances, I hereby grant a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses.
As per medical documents, the injured Tripti Kalra has suffered simple injuries.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.25,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said MACT No. 510/2020 Ravi Kalra Vs. Harsh Sharma period of her treatment and immobility.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs. 50,000/- under this head.
